A private rushed into a general's office in a hurry. "Sir, I'm back from my reconnaissance assignment. You *have* to see this," he exclaimed.

"This had better be important!" the general shouted, offended that his subordinate had broken military protocol and stormed straight into his private quarters.

"Believe me, I've stumbled upon the discovery of the century." He placed the laptop - a top-of-the-range custom-built device issued by the armed forces - on top of the general's desk and folded the device out. He booted up a 3D map, running on bespoke military software.

Surveying the map briefly, the general seemed unimpressed. "This is what you barged into my office for? A simulation of a neighboring country?"

"Yes, this is that country, or at least what we see of it," replied the private, panning the camera downwards until it ended up clipping through the terrain of a region situated north of the capital. "But look below the surface and you will find something mind-boggling!"

The general gasped. "A massive bunker network? Inside that country?"

"That's what they want you to think," explained the private, as he moved the camera deeper into the underground network. "This isn't a bunker at all. This is an underground metropolis, and a very well-decorated one at that."

"You see those floors?" he asked, pointing towards the floors of the long, twisting corridors of the underground city. "Those are paved with marble."

"And if you went towards the center of this huge metropolis," the private elaborated, panning the camera several dozen miles north-east into another region, "then you will find their source of power. Geothermal energy. The cause of all these earthquakes. That means it's not nuclear tests they were running..."

The general stopped his subordinate and picked up the laptop. "That will do. What you found today will change our understanding of our neighbors for decades to come. Good work."

The general then paused as he was about to step out of the office. "Can you do me a single favor though?"

"Yes, sir!" 

The general pulled out a revolver, and in a single motion of his right arm, shot the private in the forehead. The bullet wound killed the private instantly, and dropped his lifeless corpse to the floor.

I'd love to see a large gaming company start a second development team for a popular MMORPG and employ some of the people working on the largest private servers, to establish official classic, expansion, and legacy realms and perform any necessary maintenance and bug fixes.

Another gaming company pretty much did the same thing with their classic version of a popular MMORPG when they shut down a private server that attempted to emulate an earlier era of the game. They took on-board the feedback of how many players disliked the newer version and its various changes, saw that the private server was gaining a lot of hype, and gave their fanbase what they wanted.

Fun fact, the classic version is now the *most popular* iteration of the game, regularly managing more active players at once than the newer version, and that is only set to grow even further when the development team plans a phased-release of brand new content exclusive to the classic version which will increase the size of the game world immensely.

That's right, the classic version is so popular that the company is releasing *new* content for that version of the game. While I won't go so far as to say the large gaming company needs to release new classic/expansion content, a launch of legacy servers running on older versions of the game client is what they need to be doing with their MMORPG.

If the large gaming company made an old-school client available and allowed subscribers to download the older clients and experience the game as it was originally intended, I would resub in a heartbeat. Hell, even if they did what the other company did and hired a few extra developers to produce new content for the classic game such as the originally intended raid and a slew of cut zones and islands from that era, then I can see legacy realms eclipsing the current release realms with absolute ease.

It's quite sad that you can only experience the previous game world, and the original class abilities, talents, and itemization which fueled the game these days by playing on a private server. Meanwhile on the retail version, any content outside of the automated group finder and the main raid remains abandoned, and cannot be experienced at its originally intended difficulty level even if you could 'level down' your character like in other MMORPGs thanks to years and years of immense power creep through poorly designed game updates.

The large gaming company says it's too hard, or 'the technology simply isn't there', but there are people who have reverse-engineered the older clients and managed to run a slew of private servers which have both emulated and built upon a similar experience.

I'm very, very skeptical of the hate and accusations of viewbotting towards a certain streamer for one very big reason.

A well-known gaming community has re-listed this streamer as a featured content creator after a six month probation. Full post on the community forum linked and quoted below:

> A Decision Regarding the Streamer's Probation

> In March 2015, the community decided to remove this streamer from the featured list after revelations of viewbotting. Our original decision was made due to the fact that there was no way to establish the streamer's actual viewership count and whether it would have qualified for featured status. There was a possibility that the streamer acquired featured status solely because of the suspected bots, which aided in amassing more legitimate viewers. The original investigation showed that the stream was a target of botting, but there was no way to establish beyond reasonable doubt who was responsible for the botting.

> Based on the evidence provided, we decided that the best course of action was to remove the streamer from our featured list and put them on a 6 month probation. At the same time, the streamer promised to change their content and attempt to clear the accusations. During this time, they remained a spotlighted streamer on a popular platform.

> Now that the probation period has expired, we must revisit our decision and decide whether or not to refeature them. This has been a very high profile case, so we do not take this decision lightly. We have placed the burden of proof on the streamer to show that their content is clean and that the problem is past them.

Ahhh, a typical "Just make more money" argument. For a lot of people, this simply isn't an option.

Let's say you work in retail or customer service and earn the minimum wage, which a lot of people do. The average full-time contract in many countries is for 37.5 hours per week, and the national minimum wage in the UK is £7.20 (for a worker over 25 years old, whereas it gets even lower for anyone below that age.)

Hence, a 25+ worker can earn £270 per week, £14,040 per year, or £1,170 per month in pre-tax pay.

Now let's subtract taxation and National Insurance contributions from this figure. This gives us a net annual wage (rounded to nearest penny) of £12,714.40 per year, £1,059.53 per month, £244.51 per week, or £6.52 per hour.

Since employees are usually paid at the end of the month, we're now concerned with the net monthly figure of £1,059.53. Let's subtract the average monthly energy bill on a small house/flat from that figure, which is £61 per month, then subtract food (£140) and internet (£20) from that monthly bill, on the assumption that the worker is living the austere lifestyle of a student.

This means that we now have an income of £838.53 per month after taxation and basic necessities (gas/electricity, groceries/food, internet connection, which is almost mandatory in today's society, and is required to play online games, so we're factoring this in as well.)

Since we're now concerned with the disposable income of a minimum wage 25+ worker, let's compare the monthly income of £838.53 per month to average rent prices in various regions.

* Greater London - There is no way that anybody on a salary that low can live in this area with its average rent costs of £1,560 per month. This region is just *that* heavily price gouged due to overpopulation, gentrification, and heavy demand for properties. Even most residents can barely afford to live here on their increased average salaries compared to the rest of the country.

* South East England - Perhaps if you're lucky enough to find a cheap property far away from the capital to rent, you could maybe live a very austere life in this region. Otherwise, good luck, because it is populated pretty highly with workers who commute into the capital on a regular basis.

* South West - At £872 per month, the average property in this region is pretty unaffordable and will leave you living an incredibly austere lifestyle.

* East Anglia - At £809 per month, we finally have a point where we can calculate the percentage of disposable income that a realm transfer priced at £17 would be: 838.53 - 809 = 29.53, and (17 / 29.53) *100 = ~57.57% of your disposable income.

With the rest of monthly rent prices being very close to the West Midlands figure, and being at most ~£150 lower, let's not calculate the rest. * Low wages. Unless you're working for an insourced customer service department, or are in a developing region where wages are significantly lower, don't expect to be paid above the minimum wage, especially when doing basic tasks.

* Irate and abusive customers. It's often worse on the phone than in person. You will encounter this regardless of how good or bad the organization is, and you'll soon become desensitized to it, as long as you don't take it personally.

* Having to escalate your call to a supervisor frequently. Sometimes, there is very little you can do to manage a call if the person on the other end is unhappy with the process - no matter how much you try to make it sound better.

* Favouritism. Some customer service centers have notoriously poor company cultures. Generally, it's the inbound ones that frequently receive negative reviews online that you need to be cautious of. In these environments, don't expect to advance unless you've formed strong friendships. By the way, I would suggest avoiding outbound work unless it involves courtesy calls and not telemarketing.

* Lots of stress. This increases even more if you're in any kind of supervisory position like senior agent, team leader, etc.

I'm very reluctant to get back into this MMORPG. I haven't even reached Level 50 yet and I find it an absolute slog to go through the story quests, especially when:

* The story quests that you're forced to do to unlock new zones, dungeons, trials, etc., often outlevel you frequently, often forcing you to participate in public events for 2/3 of a level to get enough XP to meet the requirement of the next quest. By the way, a lot of mid-level zones require groups to complete these events, so if there aren't players around, you're stuck doing repetitive side quests for a fraction of the XP.

* It's often near-impossible to find groups for certain trials. I actually had to get max level players to help me in the trials past a certain boss because nobody was queuing for them.

* The game's story quests are repetitive and formulaic. All the quest lines before Level 50 can be boiled down into a formula. 1. You seek assistance from a leader 2. He doesn't trust you and forces you to go on all kinds of tedious fetch and 'kill x monsters' quests 3. You finally earn the assistance you should have received in the first place and go to a location. 4. The quest line concludes in a mandatory dungeon run.

* The game forces you to finish the story quests to progress further. Want to do the next expansion's content? You have to finish the 1 - 49 story quests, then complete the endgame story quests released between patches just to unlock expansion content. Imagine how many subscribers a popular MMORPG would lose if they forced players to finish all the quests in a previous expansion's major zones just to advance further.

* For the next expansion, the company is selling level and quest completion boosts, but they're sold separately, aren't packaged in any way with the expansion, and are somehow more expensive than a similar boost offered by another popular MMORPG.
